tasks.short: Deliver written orders to the kitchens and serve the food when ready.

steps.what: Carry written orders into the kitchens
Cook starts the food from that kitchen ticket
Watch the pass until the plates are ready
Pick up the plated food at the pass
Serve the ready food at the counter

tasks.design: The {OTHER} till sends the order ticket to a printer or screen in the kitchen. The counter worker still picks up plated food and serves it. Native ticket routing is tested before any custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: The kitchen is a few steps away and the ticket is one slip, so carrying it felt faster than keeping a printer fed.
tasks.enabler_now: The till can already print or show the same ticket at the station. Switching that route on is configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Plates are hot, orders stack at the pass, and a missing item is seen by eye. A printer jam sends the worker back with the paper.
tasks.human_edge: The worker sees a plate that does not match the ticket and does not hand it over.
tasks.altitude: The counter worker still stands at the pass. The walk with a paper ticket drops when the kitchen printer is on. Picking up plates and serving them stays, and the worker still refuses a plate that does not match the ticket.

reach.task: Start food from the kitchen ticket
reach.learn: Read the printed or on-screen ticket as the order, and ask only when an item is missing.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere can send an order to the kitchen through the point-of-sale, which is the paper-ticket walk this task removes.
Carrying plated food and handing it to the guest stays with the person at the pass.

assumptions: This task starts when a written or rung order already exists and ends when the food is in the guest's hands. It does not include taking the order or cooking.

Kitchen ticket fields are item code, quantity, modifier code and order number, produced by the till when the order is rung. If the till cannot route to the kitchen printer, the worker carries the paper ticket.
Native ticket routing is tested before custom code.
unknowns: Whether this site's till can route a ticket to a kitchen printer or station screen.
How often the kitchen printer jams during a rush.
research_questions: What share of orders is still walked in on paper because the station printer is off?
Does the kitchen already show the same ticket the counter rang?

already_counted.description: Watching the pass, picking up plates and serving them
Cook starting the food from the ticket

incremental.description: Reprint a kitchen ticket when the printer fails.
Kitchen lead checks that each item still prints to the right station.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central case drops only the walk with the paper ticket. Plates stay with the worker. If the kitchen already prints tickets, that walk is short and saving sits at the low end. A printer jam puts the walk back. The one hour for a reprint is already off the central figure.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise employees and train them on the station.

steps.what: Watch employees while supervising the station
Coach employees through station training on the line
Write the training note for that employee
Area supervisor agrees the employee finished training

tasks.design: A station checklist in {DOCS} replaces the handwritten training line. Watching the line and coaching the starter stay with the counter worker. The area supervisor still agrees that the employee finished.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training is a few minutes beside the fryer, and the note is a line in a book.
tasks.enabler_now: A one-page station checklist can live in {DOCS}.
tasks.still_hard: A new starter's hands, the pace of the line, and hot food. The area supervisor still has to watch once.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer sees a grip or a skipped hand-wash that a tick list does not show.
tasks.altitude: The week is still coaching on the line. The handwritten book becomes a short tick list. The counter worker does not gain the right to sign off a new starter alone.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of food preparation and serving workers
reach.task: Agree that a starter finished the station
reach.learn: Read the station checklist and still watch the starter once before signing.

evidence.claim: A one-page checklist in a document store can replace a handwritten training line. The watching and the coaching stay.
A per-person sales log in the till can be a tool to monitor staff, so the works council must consent. This design adds no sales log.

assumptions: This task is on-shift coaching and the training note. It does not include hiring, rosters or pay.
Checklist fields are station name, employee id, date and a tick per station step, produced by the trainer. If {DOCS} has no checklist, the paper note stays.
The note is not a performance score and is not a sales log. Works-council consent applies if the named note is later used to judge the person.
unknowns: Whether the works council treats a named training note as monitoring.
Whether the site still keeps the training book on paper.
research_questions: Who may see a named station checklist after the shift?
Does the area supervisor already sign the paper book, or is the note never read?

already_counted.description: Watching the station, coaching on the line, and ticking the note
Area supervisor agreeing the starter finished

incremental.description: Correct a tick that landed on the wrong station step.
Area supervisor keeps the station checklist current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central case shortens only the handwritten note. Watching and coaching stay. If the site keeps a paper book, saving is zero, which is the low end. The half hour for a wrong tick is already off the central figure.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notify kitchen personnel of shortages or special orders.

steps.what: Hear shortages or special orders at the counter
Key a listed shortage onto the kitchen ticket
Notify kitchen personnel of an unlisted special order
Kitchen personnel confirm they can meet that order
Tell the guest the shortage or special-order result

tasks.design: Item buttons on the {OTHER} till put a fixed modifier or an item-off flag on the kitchen ticket. An unlisted special, or an allergen the menu record does not list, is still spoken to kitchen personnel. Native till buttons are tested before any custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Special requests were a shout because the till had no modifier, and shortages changed minute to minute.
tasks.enabler_now: Item buttons can carry a fixed modifier list and an item-off flag onto the kitchen ticket.
tasks.still_hard: A request in the guest's own words, and an allergen the menu record does not list.
tasks.human_edge: The worker hears a request to leave nuts out and does not treat it as a button called no sauce.

ambition.what: Mark an item off on the till as soon as the tray is empty, so the next guest is not sold food the kitchen cannot make.

tasks.altitude: Listed shortages and modifiers go out on the kitchen ticket. The counter worker still speaks an unlisted special, and still does not clear an allergen that is missing from the menu record.

reach.task: Confirm a shortage or a special order
reach.learn: Read a listed modifier on the ticket, and answer a spoken special that is not on the list.

evidence.claim: A till can put a keyed modifier or an item-off flag on the kitchen ticket when the modifier is a fixed button.
Guests must be told about the 14 allergens in unpacked food. Spoken information is allowed when a notice says they can ask. A guessed ingredient list is not acceptable.
In 2022, 41 percent of 9,407 inspected horeca businesses complied with the allergen-information duty.

assumptions: This task is kitchen notification. It does not include explaining the dish or cooking it.
Fields are a modifier code and an item-off flag on the order, produced by the counter worker from a fixed list. Free text is not parsed.
An unlisted request, or an allergen with no line on the menu record, is spoken to the cook.
Native till buttons are tested before custom code.
unknowns: Whether the menu record lists the 14 allergens on each item.
What share of special requests is already a button, against free speech.
research_questions: Which shortages can the till mark off before the next guest orders?
Where does the counter worker read the allergen line when a guest asks?

already_counted.description: Hearing the request, speaking an unlisted special, and telling the guest
Cook confirming the kitchen can meet the order

incremental.description: Fix a modifier keyed on the wrong item.
Cook updates which items are off before the next rush.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central case removes the shout only for modifiers and shortages that are already buttons. Unlisted specials and the guest conversation stay. If most requests are free speech, saving falls toward the low end. The two hours for a wrong modifier are already off the central figure.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take customers' orders and write ticket stubs for filled orders.

steps.what: Customers state their orders at the counter
Listen and repeat the ordered items back
Write ordered items on paper tickets
Ring the ordered items on the counter till
Hand ticket stubs to customers for filled orders
Store the priced ticket lines for that order

tasks.design: Item buttons on the {OTHER} till, and a guest order that already carries item codes, write the lines the pen wrote, and the till prints the stub number. The counter worker still repeats a spoken order. Native till buttons and the existing order link are tested before any custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: The queue is face to face, and a pen and a numbered stub were enough when the till was only a cash drawer.
tasks.enabler_now: Item buttons and a guest order screen can write the same lines the pen wrote, and the till can print the stub number.
tasks.still_hard: A guest who changes the order mid-sentence, a till that is down, and repeating the order so the guest hears it.
tasks.human_edge: The worker hears a mumbled item and an allergy in the same breath and does not tap the wrong button.

ambition.what: Guests in the dining room send an order from their own screen instead of queueing at the counter.

tasks.altitude: Handwriting the second ticket drops, and a guest screen can ring its own lines. Repeating a spoken order stays. The counter worker does not gain the right to guess an allergen that is not on the menu record.

reach.task: Take an order away from the counter
reach.learn: Send the same item codes the counter till uses, and still repeat a spoken change.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere lets a guest read descriptions and allergens, order and pay, and sends that order to the kitchen through the point-of-sale.
Orderli takes a QR order and payment and links that order to the till the site already uses, including Lightspeed, unTill, Vectron or MplusKASSA.

The Lightspeed vendor reports about 8 percent more transactions from Order Anywhere, and Fitzbillies reports 20 percent higher spend per QR order than at the counter. These figures are sales, not labour time.
If the order screen shows allergens, they must come from the menu record. Spoken information is allowed when a notice says guests can ask.

assumptions: This task ends when the stub is in the guest's hand. It does not include payment or carrying food.

Fields are item code, quantity, modifier code and order number, produced by the till from button presses or from a guest order that arrives with those fields. The handwritten ticket is the fallback when the till is down.
Prices on the menu include tax. This task does not add a tax line.
Native till buttons and the existing order link are tested before custom code. There is no guest chatbot and no per-worker order count.
unknowns: What share of orders is spoken at the counter against sent from a guest screen.
Whether the menu record lists allergens per item for the order screen.
research_questions: What share of tickets is still handwritten when the till is up?
Does a guest order already arrive as item codes the till can store?

already_counted.description: Repeating the spoken order, ringing the lines, and handing the stub
Guests stating orders at the counter

incremental.description: Correct a mis-keyed item before the ticket prints.
Menu owner keeps the item buttons matched to the menu.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central case removes the second handwriting and shortens ringing where a guest screen already sent item codes. Repeating the order stays. If guests still all queue and speak, only the paper ticket goes and saving sits near the low end. The two hours for a mis-keyed item are already off the central figure. The vendor's transaction and spend figures are not labour time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still at the counter and the pass. Carrying a paper ticket into the kitchen, handwriting a second ticket, and shouting a listed modifier shrink. Coaching on the station stays. The counter worker does not gain the right to clear an allergen that is not on the menu record, or to sign off a new starter alone.
reach: Waiters and waitresses can send the same kitchen ticket from the floor instead of walking a slip to the pass.
Fast food cooks read the ticket on the station screen and only ask when the modifier is not on the list.
First-line supervisors of food preparation and serving workers read a station checklist instead of a handwritten book, and still watch the starter once.
skills_to_grow: Tell a listed modifier from one that must be spoken to the kitchen.
Tick a station checklist without turning it into a score of the person.
Hand the guest the order number the till printed, and still repeat a spoken order back.
role.ambitious_version: The till holds the menu buttons, the modifier list and the station checklist. A standard order reaches the kitchen without a paper ticket, and a listed shortage shows on that ticket. The counter worker still listens, still carries the plates, and still coaches a new starter on the line. An allergen that is not on the menu record is still a conversation with the cook.
